subject: Retention mirroring & on-demand audit snapshot delivery
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@medicosys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicosys.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Retention mirroring and on-demand audit snapshot delivery

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG review we need a clear proposal for how Redwood can provide (1) a customer-copy of admin/audit activity (retention mirroring) and (2) on-demand snapshots of the full admin activity ledger with attested manifests and checksums.

Key asks from MedicoSys security:
- Which event classes are included in a full export (operator actions, role changes, API keys, self-service admin UI, system automated remediations)?
- Default retention windows and ability to mirror (push) a copy to our S3 or to an SFTP we control.
- Export formats (NDJSON/CSV), delivery packaging (tar.gz), and checksums (sha256) + signed manifest.
- SLA: on-demand delivery objective (we usually request 24h, with 4h emergency tier).
- Redaction/PII handling and sample redaction process for shared bundles.

We'd like a short proposal and estimated timeline (initial snapshot + recurring mirror cadence), and a one-page summary we can attach to the SIG questionnaire.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Security Lead, MedicoSys

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@medicosys.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention mirroring and on-demand audit snapshot delivery

Jane — thanks, this is clear. I've looped in Karthik (infra) and Vanessa (legal/partnerships). High level proposal below; Karthik will follow up with technical details.

Proposal (summary):
- Scope: export includes operator/admin actions, audit log of API calls that mutate state (role changes, key generation/revocation, config changes), system-initiated escalations, and access-grant events. Excludes ephemeral KV cache contents and model-inference request payloads unless flagged in the contract.
- Formats: NDJSON for event bodies, CSV manifest for quick review, gzipped tar bundles. Each bundle comes with sha256 and md5 checksums; we will also provide a signed manifest (service account signature).
- Delivery options: push to customer S3 (we support cross-account replication via a temporary write role) or SFTP drop (instructions attached: sftp_instructions.pdf).
- Retention mirroring: canonical copy retained in Redwood for 365d by default; we offer a mirror window to customer S3 for the same period. Longer retention (up to 7 years) available by contract (cold archive).
- On-demand snapshots: standard SLA 24 hours for full export; expedited 4-hour retrieval available as a paid add-on.
- Redaction: PII redaction done via agreed scrubbing rules; we can provide a sample redaction report with the snapshot.

Next steps: Karthik will send the export manifest schema and a recommended cadence matrix (daily vs hourly deltas). If that aligns, Vanessa will prepare Appendix E (audit log delivery) language for the contract.

I'll target initial snapshot delivery within 3 business days after we finalize SFTP/S3 handshake and signing keys.

—Jonas
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Jane Park <jane.park@medicosys.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention mirroring and on-demand audit snapshot delivery

Hi all — a few technical specifics to cement the SLA and expected artifact sizes/times.

What we log (included in exports):
- admin_action events: {timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, before, after, request_id, ip_address, user_agent}
- api_admin events (token use / key rotation): {timestamp, principal, endpoint, params_redacted, request_id}
- role_change events (grants, revocations) with before/after role blobs
- system_event entries for automated escalations and scheduled job runs (for provenance)

What we do NOT include by default: model input/output, low-level GPU telemetry, ephemeral cache contents. If MedicoSys requires specific inference payloads for audit, we'll need a separate DPA addendum.

Packaging and transport:
- Export format: NDJSON per-event file, compressed as audit_snapshot_YYYYMMDD.tar.gz. Manifest is CSV with event counts, size, first/last timestamps, and sha256 for each file.
- Checksums: we provide md5 and sha256; manifest itself is signed with our service key (we can exchange a verification public key).
- Delivery: S3 cross-account role is fastest for recurring mirrors (we push small daily deltas + weekly full snapshots). SFTP is supported for one-off snapshots but expect longer transfer time for multi-GB bundles.

Sizing and SLAs:
- Typical medium customer: daily delta ~200MB compressed; weekly full ~2–6GB depending on operator volume.
- 24-hour on-demand: we can attach and produce an export within 24h in 95% of cases. 4-hour expedited: we reserve and prioritize compute; success depends on bundle size and network egress (expedite fee applies).

Redaction options: server-side scrubbing rules applied before bundling; we produce a redaction log indicating which fields were removed or masked.

I'll attach the export_policy_matrix.xlsx and a sample manifest (see attachments). Happy to run a small test export to your SFTP before we finalize the contract language.

—Karthik
Engineering Manager, Inference Ops

From: Jane Park <jane.park@medicosys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention mirroring and on-demand audit snapshot delivery

Thanks Karthik — that answers most questions. Two clarifications before we route to legal:
1) Proof-of-custody: we need a signed manifest that includes the sha256 for each file and the identity of the operator who initiated the export. Is the service key signature acceptable, or do you provide a notarized statement?
2) Redaction cert: for any customer-shared bundle we require a redaction certificate indicating the exact scrubbing rules applied and a sample of 10 events pre/post redaction.

Also, for the 24h SLA we want an RTO/RPO statement we can include in the SIG: maximum generation time, and the window in which you guarantee completeness. If you can draft a 1-paragraph SLA snippet we can attach, that'll speed review.

If possible, schedule the test export next Tuesday (2027-04-06) to our SFTP test endpoint. We will provide the credentials once the handshake is done.

—Jane

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@medicosys.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention mirroring and on-demand audit snapshot delivery

Jane — great, appreciate the clear asks. Finalizing plan below and next steps.

Final plan (agreed):
- Initial test export: Tue 2027-04-06 -> SFTP test endpoint (Jonas to provide creds and handoff doc).
- Production initial snapshot: target Fri 2027-04-09 (full bundle + signed manifest + sha256 checksums).
- Recurring mirror: daily deltas pushed to customer S3 (cross-account write role); weekly full snapshot retained 365 days by default.
- SLA language (draft): "Standard on-demand audit export: Redwood will produce and deliver a complete audit snapshot (as defined in Appendix E) within 24 hours of request in 95% of cases. Expedited delivery (4-hour objective) is available as a billable premium; feasibility is subject to export size and network constraints."
- Proof-of-custody: we will include signed manifests (service account signature) and provide an auditable chain-of-custody CSV. If notarization is required we can route to legal and provide options.
- Redaction cert: we will include the redaction report and a 10-event pre/post sample for each shared bundle.

Attachments included in this thread: sftp_instructions.pdf, export_policy_matrix.xlsx. I will upload the sample audit_snapshot_20270402.tar.gz and export_manifest.csv to the Drive folder and share after the test export.

Next actions (short):
1) Jane: provide SFTP test endpoint and contact for credentials exchange.
2) Karthik: confirm estimate for full snapshot size and expedite fee ranges.
3) Vanessa: draft Appendix E language and the 1-paragraph SLA blurb for SIG.

I'll follow up after the test export. Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

—Jonas
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
